transcript:
Header:
Date/Time: 2026-11-30 17:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Location: Zoom (recording)
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Owen Patel (Redwood CSM); Sarah Blake (HelioHealth Head of Partnerships), Dr. Amit Rao (HelioHealth CTO), Lena Ortiz (HelioHealth Legal Ops), Marcus Yu (HelioHealth Sales)

Summary: Rapid partner ops sprint to deconflict overlapping opportunities in EMEA + US, align on a repeatable co-sell playbook for healthcare pilots, confirm legal/data residency asks, and assign owners for a joint pilot and exec review. Conversation covered marketplace listings, pricing split hypotheses, EU data residency (on-prem/vpc), and technical perf baseline for inference.

Topics Covered:
- Pipeline deconflict and prioritization (3 deals flagged)
- Co-sell vs referral economics and suggested revenue split ranges
- Technical constraints: VPC/private deployment for PHI, latency targets, model variants
- Legal checklist: SOC2/ISO, audit logs, data retention, KMS/HSM expectations
- Next steps and owners for pilot runbook and exec alignment

Action items (captured in metadata above)

Transcript Body:
[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone, thanks for jumping in. quick icebreaker then we'll run through the three deals on the board.
[00:12] Sarah Blake: yeah thanks Maya, appreciate it. we have a tight window on two of these and wanted to make sure we're not stepping on each other's toes.
[00:20] Diego Alvarez: cool, i'll give a short tech status then we'll triage by revenue and compliance risk.
[00:27] Marcus Yu: just to flag, the EU hospital chain is our highest revenue potential but also most constrained on data residency.
[00:35] Maya Chen: got it. ok deal A is EU hospital chain, deal B is US payer pilot, deal C is a med-device partner in APAC. Sarah, can you confirm priority?
[00:48] Sarah Blake: priority is A then B then C, but if Redwood has a fast VPC pattern for EU we can advance A quickly. otherwise we'll run B in parallel.
[00:59] Diego Alvarez: on the VPC/on-prem ask — we have our Redwood Private patterns: VPC deployments with customer-managed subnets and optional on-prem package. latency depends on model size and kv cache warm-up, typically 50–200ms median for optimized 7B variants, 100–400ms for 13B depending on batch.
[01:22] Dr. Amit Rao: that 50–200ms is optimistic; hospital requires sub-200ms for triage UI. also need to confirm PHI cannot leave region and keys must be customer-managed.
[01:36] Diego Alvarez: understood. we can propose a dedicated capacity reservation for EU to bound latency and ensure KMS integration for key control.
[01:45] Owen Patel: from partner ops side, we need to get HelioHealth RevOps into the loop for revenue split conversations — do we have a starting point on economics?
[01:55] Maya Chen: quick thought: for direct co-sell EMR integrations we typically propose 60/40 to partner when they're bringing sales + integration; referral smaller. but thats negotiable based on enablement investment.
[02:10] Sarah Blake: 60/40 sounds reasonable as a starting point, but we need a clear enablement play + joint win criteria.
[02:18] Marcus Yu: also we need to be mindful of existing resellers in APAC — don't want channel conflict.
[02:24] Diego Alvarez: technical question for Sarah/Amit, will the EU hospital allow us to run a small LLM cache in their private subnet or do they want fully air-gapped model weights?
[02:35] Dr. Amit Rao: for the pilot we can host in their VPC and allow model weights in a sealed image, but no outbound telemetry. audit logging must be delivered to their SIEM.
[02:46] Maya Chen: great that's workable. ok let's triage the three deals — i'll summarize risk and next steps for each.
[02:54] [Screen share: pipeline board]
[03:03] Maya Chen: Deal A (EU hospital chain) — high ARR, high compliance risk. owners: Sarah/Maya; technical SE: Diego. immediate asks: legal checklist, dedicated EU capacity quote, pilot perf baseline.
[03:18] Sarah Blake: timeline: they want an exec pilot kickoff before 2027-01-15.
[03:24] Diego Alvarez: i'll estimate cost/TCO and perf with two model variants: 7B-int8 optimized and 13B-q4 if needed; will include expected latency ranges and autoscaling knobs.
[03:38] Maya Chen: Deal B (US payer) — moderate ARR, lower compliance friction, great TTV. owner Marcus + Owen; can run hosted Redwood API for initial pilot with strict retention policies.
[03:52] Owen Patel: for B we should propose a 6-week pilot with SLAs for uptime and token spend cap. also we can demonstrate cost/perf tradeoff via a short benchmark.
[04:05] Maya Chen: Deal C (APAC med-device) — smaller but strategic for channel play. need partner conflict review.
[04:14] Sarah Blake: APAC partner is a bit touchy; we'll hold off until we confirm non-conflict.
[04:20] Diego Alvarez: moving onto compliance and legal asks — Lena, can you highlight must-haves from HelioHealth legal?
[04:27] Lena Ortiz: sure; SOC2 Type II or equivalent, ISO27001 preferred, contractual audit rights, KMS for key management and no model telemetry outside region. data retention max 30 days for PII unless consented. also we need liability caps and indemnities spelled out for PHI processing.
[04:47] Maya Chen: Redwood can provide SOC2 report, ISO attestation in progress, and we support customer-managed KMS and HSM integrations. we have an MSA addendum template for PHI that we can share.
[04:59] Lena Ortiz: good. can you also include sample audit log formats? their security team will ask for that.
[05:06] Diego Alvarez: yes, we'll export structured audit logs with request id, model id, route, timestamp, and hash of payload — though the transcription occasionally mangles header names — but we'll include schema.
[05:22] Marcus Yu: quick pricing question: if we run Dedicated reserved capacity in EU, how do we split cost for the pilot vs expected revenue share?
[05:31] Owen Patel: two options: Redwood bill partner for dedicated capacity and include as OPEX in rev-split, or we amortize the capacity cost across pilot seat charges and adjust split. we can draft both scenarios.
[05:44] Sarah Blake: we prefer a clean split approach; partner wants predictable cost.
[05:49] Maya Chen: we'll prepare revenue model scenarios. Diego, can you include shot-gun numbers for e.g., 6-week pilot est cost at two capacity levels?
[05:58] Diego Alvarez: yes, i'll provide conservative and aggressive capacity estimates.
[06:05] [Silence, background typing]
[06:14] Dr. Amit Rao: slightly off-topic: for ML quality, what tooling do you provide for regression monitoring and evals? we need to ensure no model drift in clinical prompts.
[06:23] Diego Alvarez: Redwood Optimize includes eval hooks, prompt set monitoring, and regression alerts. we can tie it to a prompt corpus and threshold-based alerts; we also support model rollbacks. incase of drift, we have canary policies.
[06:39] Dr. Amit Rao: good. can we export evaluation metrics to our dashboard?
[06:44] Diego Alvarez: yes via webhooks or direct export to S3/Secure bucket.
[06:50] Sarah Blake: ok moving towards wrap — what are the key blockers to starting the EU pilot next month?
[06:56] Maya Chen: legal checklist completion, dedicated EU capacity quote, and HelioHealth signoff on data residency/KMS. once we have those we can lock a Jan kickoff.
[07:08] Lena Ortiz: i also want to confirm encryption-in-transit, at-rest, and HSM key custody model.
[07:14] Diego Alvarez: we support TLS1.3 in transit and envelope encryption at rest; customer-managed keys via KMS, and we can support HSM-backed key stores for the private deployment.
[07:26] Marcus Yu: competitive callouts — customer asked about Anthropic safety stack and Bedrock integration. how do we position Redwood?
[07:35] Maya Chen: Redwood's pitch is production-grade inference with unified ops across hosted/dedicated/private — emphasize predictable latency, cost controls, and co-sell support + partner enablement.
[07:47] Owen Patel: also highlight the joint enablement kit and partner marketplace listing to help deals accelerate.
[07:54] Sarah Blake: sounds good.
[07:57] [Long silence, note taking]
[08:10] Maya Chen: final recap: Maya to send playbook + marketplace link by 12/03; Diego to send perf/capacity doc by 12/07; Owen to draft revenue-split scenarios and intro to pricing lead by 12/06; Lena to return legal checklist by 12/04. schedule exec sync week of 12/14.
[08:33] Dr. Amit Rao: ok thanks, that works.
[08:37] Marcus Yu: let's aim to get the MSA addendum on deck early, i'll push internally.
[08:42] Maya Chen: awesome, thanks all. we'll follow up in the thread with the docs. bye.
[08:47] [Meeting ends — recording stopped]

Notes on transcription quality: occasional OCR-like name mangles (e.g., 'Maya' sometimes transcribed as 'Major' in older exports), and some technical terms (KV cache, HSM) may appear as 'K V cash' or 'H S M' in some lines; manual review advised for legal artifacts.
